# Enterobacterales

> *How do harmless gut residents and dangerous strains of the same species differ?*

::: {.callout-note}
## In preparation
This chapter will follow the layout of [*Gram-positive cocci*](gram-positive-cocci.qmd). The plan:
:::

| Part of the chapter | Plan |
|---|---|
| The group in one sentence | Gram-negative rods that ferment sugars, cope with or without oxygen, and live in the gut |
| Sorting key | Extra genes (toxins, adhesins, capsules); lactose fermentation as a lab readout |
| Main organisms | *E. coli* (residents versus strains with extra genes), *Klebsiella* (capsule), *Salmonella* (survival inside cells) |
| Supporting organisms | *Shigella*, *Proteus*, *Yersinia* |
| Later in the course | Gut, urinary and bloodstream infections in the organ blocks; resistant strains in pharmacology |
